title: Horizontal valuation bases, relative curves and flat closure pair data
statement: A horizontal valuation base consists of a valuation domain $V$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], a specified fraction field $K$ [def-weil-field], its algebra structure $V\to K$, separable closedness of $K$ [def-kun-separably-closed], and a finite linearly ordered prime spectrum of $V$. Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ and $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ for the actual morphism induced by the algebra map [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For schemes $T,Y$ [def-pc-scheme] and $y:Y\to T$, a relative curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented morphism (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]) whose scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre] all have pure dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. For any $\eta:S\to T$, multipointed curve $P=(X,D)$ [def-trf-multipointed-curve], and $q:Y\to X$, let $q_\eta:Y\times_T S\to X\times_T S$ be the canonical base-change map and let $j:Z\to Y\times_T S$ be the pullback of the marking $D\times_T S\to X\times_T S$ along $q_\eta$, using the canonical base-change marking of [def-trf-multipointed-curve-modification]. More generally, for any $j:Z\to Y\times_T S$ and $e:E\to Y$, a flat closure datum consists of: $e$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]; equality of its kernel ideal sheaf with the kernel ideal sheaf of $Z\xrightarrow{j}Y\times_T S\to Y$; flatness and finite presentation of $E\to T$; pure dimension zero of all its fibres; and equality of the pullback of $\ker(e)$ to $Y\times_T S$ with $\ker(j)$. These are conditions on the specified maps, not an existence assertion. A relative curve datum for $y$ and such a flat closure datum define the multipointed curve with curve $Y$, marking $E$, inclusion $e$, and structure maps $y$ and $e$ followed by $y$. In the case $y=q$ followed by $X\to T$ and $j$ the pulled-back generic marking above, any $r:E\to D$ satisfying $r$ followed by $D\to T=e$ followed by $q$ followed by $X\to T$ and $r$ followed by $D\to X=e$ followed by $q$ defines the morphism of multipointed curves to $P$ with curve map $q$ and marking map $r$ [def-trf-multipointed-curve-modification]. Empty markings and empty fibres are allowed; no separatedness or properness condition is included.
